decisions.id: W106-a one rule, not a knob
decisions.summary: each tub beside a door of its building; the roof seat 0100 also attests is not drawn
decisions.why: The ranked fix itself offers 'at the wooden building's entrance' as its first alternative, and the GM's 2026-07-25/26 ruling (no part of a tub glyph in a footprint) leaves the roof seat undrawable on a plan, so the exception is implied by the GM's own words. Recording gap, not a fidelity block: the roof seat's omission is stated only in plan.md - neither the spec's wave-106 Decisions Recorded row nor 0100's drawing page says the roof seat is deliberately not drawn and why.

decisions.summary: TUB_DOOR_MAX_FT 10.5 ft, a CONVENTION from the kitchen's second tub side by side at one door
decisions.why: 0100 gives no distance; a check needs one; it is labeled CONVENTION at the code, the doc and the drawing page. Re-measured on the six sheets (judged tubs): farthest 10.4 ft (round-trip), 10.0 ft (Ochiba), 9.9 ft (Ubame).

decisions.id: W106-c1 a tagged door past the outline tolerance
decisions.summary: doors_of keeps a tagged door only within DOOR_ON_WALL_PX (6 px) of the footprint; a building whose tagged entrance stands farther out is treated as drawing no door, so its tub is not judged
decisions.why: Measured in the clone (pack_audit's own parse, doors_of at 12 px instead of 6): Hayakawa's guest house tags its entrance (rect 925,300 30x8, 'entry from the guest garden') 8 px out, so its tub at (888,210) - 35.8 ft from that door, at the NW corner - passes unjudged; Ubame's tub at (246,256) stands 49.7 ft from its building's tagged door, likewise unjudged. These are exactly the row's defect (a tub at a wall or eaves corner, not the entrance) passing because the check misreads a drawn door. Not impossible: widen the tolerance to the door glyphs the sheets actually draw, then re-seat.

decisions.id: W106-c2 a wooden building that draws no door is not judged (hand sheets and the draft's court-face fallback)
decisions.summary: a tub whose host buildings tag no door is exempt from tubs_off_their_doors; the hand sheets' tubs at such buildings were left where they stood, and the draft seats a door-less building's tub on the court face 'as before'
decisions.why: Measured: 23 of the six sheets' 77 tubs are unjudged - Hayakawa 5 of 13, Ochiba 3 of 10, Ubame 9 of 19, the county draft 2 of 14, the round-trip sheet 4 of 17 (Hoshigaoka 0 of 4). Several still stand where the row says they must not, by the sheets' own comments: Hayakawa's stables tub 'NW eaves corner', the residence east block's 'off the veranda's SE corner', the Fire Dragon shrine's 'against the east eaves'; the round-trip sheet's cinnabar workshop and clerks' room draw no door and take the old court-face seat. The ranked fix names all six sheets and says 'not at a wall or eaves corner'; the exemption is word-plausible (no door to measure to) and purpose-fatal (the defect survives on ~30% of tubs). Not physically impossible: this same wave tagged Hoshigaoka's doors precisely so its corner tubs could be judged and moved - the remedy (draw or tag the entrance of each tubbed wooden building, on the sheets and in the draft's door emission, then seat the tub beside it) was applied to one sheet and withheld from five. The figure m:wave106-tubs-at-doors misstates the same thing: 'after 0 of 13' (Hayakawa), '0 of 19' (Ubame) and the rest count unjudged tubs in the denominator as passing, while Hoshigaoka's 'before' line says '0 of 4 judged'; restate each sheet as judged / unjudged.

decisions.id: W106-c3 the bath takes the court face
decisions.summary: the draft's bath (10x8 ft, appended as a tub host beside the kitchen) carries no door and its tub falls back to the court face
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from c2 (MODE 1's seam rule): a bath entered from the house has no exterior entrance to stand water at, so the entrance seat is physically absent - provided the bath is in fact drawn with no outside door. The plan does not distinguish this case; it should be recorded as its own decision (spec Decisions Recorded and the point of change) when c2 is fixed, or the bath given its door.

decisions.id: W106-d2 no clear seat beside a door
decisions.summary: the draft falls back to the court face when a door-tagged building has no clear seat beside or round the corner from its door
decisions.why: Applies only where the seat is physically unavailable, and because the building's doors are tagged, tubs_off_their_doors reports such a tub rather than passing it silently; the county draft has none (12 judged tubs at 7.0-7.2 ft).

decisions.id: W106-corner round the corner for a short face
decisions.summary: a face too short for a tub beside its door (the gatehouse's 12 ft end) takes one round the corner nearest the door, still within 10.5 ft
decisions.why: Still beside the entrance by the same measure; labeled UNRESEARCHED at docs/buildings.md.

decisions.id: W106-d Ochiba's residence tub at the family's door
decisions.summary: the residence's tub at the notch corner by the family's door, ~5 ft, not by the guests' stepping stone
decisions.why: The residence's only drawn door is the family's (an uchi-genkan in function; 0100's original is genkan-saki); the guests' way in is a stepping stone at the reception's veranda, not a door, and the formal genkan is on the office hall. Re-measured 4.9 ft. Aside: the sheet's tub-layer comment still reads 'sits AGAINST its building at an eaves corner/downspout' and the pass-2/3 comments describe corner seats - stale against the new rule.

decisions.summary: the drawing page's 'the kitchen's two one either side of its door' not reworded
